name: Brown planthopper (BPH)
symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck sap at the base of tillers causing yellowing and drying of circular patches known as 'hopper burn'.
management: Avoid excess nitrogen and dense planting, drain the field intermittently, and conserve natural enemies such as mirid bugs and spiders; if ETL is crossed spray imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.3 ml/litre or pymetrozine 50 WG @ 0.6 g/litre directed at the plant base.

name: Yellow stem borer
symptoms: Larvae bore into the stem causing 'dead heart' during the vegetative stage and 'white ear head' at the reproductive stage.
management: Use resistant varieties, clip and destroy egg masses, install pheromone traps @ 5/ha and release Trichogramma japonicum; for severe infestation apply cartap hydrochloride 4G @ 25 kg/ha or chlorantraniliprole 0.4G @ 4 kg/ha.

name: Rice leaf folder
symptoms: Larvae fold leaves longitudinally and scrape green tissue leaving white streaks, reducing photosynthetic area.
management: Avoid excess nitrogen, keep field bunds clean and conserve parasitoids; spray chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @ 0.3 ml/litre or cartap hydrochloride 50 SP @ 2 g/litre if damage exceeds the ETL.

name: Rice blast
symptoms: Spindle-shaped, grey-centred lesions with brown margins appear on leaves; neck blast causes node/neck rot leading to chaffy panicles.
management: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen and treat seed with carbendazim 2 g/kg; spray tricyclazole 75 WP @ 0.6 g/litre or isoprothiolane 40 EC @ 1.5 ml/litre at boot leaf and 50% flowering stage.

name: Sheath blight
symptoms: Irregular greyish-green water-soaked lesions appear on the leaf sheath near the waterline, enlarging and coalescing to give a scalded appearance.
management: Avoid dense planting and excess nitrogen, maintain balanced potash and remove weeds/stubble; spray hexaconazole 5 EC @ 2 ml/litre or validamycin 3L @ 2.5 ml/litre at early symptom appearance.

name: Bacterial leaf blight (rice)
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions start at leaf tips/margins and turn yellow to white; severe cases cause wilting of seedlings known as kresek.
management: Use resistant varieties, avoid clipping seedlings before transplanting, apply balanced nitrogen and drain-dry the field intermittently; spray copper oxychloride 50 WP @ 2.5 g/litre or streptocycline 100-200 ppm with a copper fungicide.

name: Wheat yellow (stripe) rust
symptoms: Yellow-orange powdery pustules appear in stripes along the leaf veins; severe infection causes premature drying of leaves and shrivelled grain.
management: Grow resistant varieties, monitor early-sown crop and field borders; spray propiconazole 25 EC @ 1 ml/litre or tebuconazole 25.9 EC @ 1 ml/litre at first appearance and repeat after 15 days if needed.

name: Wheat aphid
symptoms: Colonies suck sap from leaves and ear heads causing yellowing, stunting and honeydew-induced sooty mould; heavy infestation shrivels grain.
management: Conserve natural enemies such as coccinellids and syrphids, avoid late sowing and excess nitrogen; spray dimethoate 30 EC @ 1.5 ml/litre or imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.3 ml/litre when aphids exceed 5-10 per tiller.

name: Termites
symptoms: Damage seeds, roots and stem base leading to wilting and drying of plants, especially under moisture-stress conditions in light soils.
management: Use well-decomposed FYM, avoid undecomposed organic matter and practise deep summer ploughing; treat seed/soil with chlorpyriphos 20 EC @ 4-5 ml/kg seed or apply fipronil 0.3 G @ 25 kg/ha in furrows.

name: Pink bollworm
symptoms: Larvae bore into flower buds and bolls, feeding on seeds and lint and causing rosette flowers and stained lint in 'double boils'.
management: Destroy crop residue after harvest, avoid ratooning, install pheromone traps @ 5/ha for monitoring and release Trichogramma; spray profenofos 50 EC @ 2 ml/litre or emamectin benzoate 5 SG @ 0.4 g/litre once ETL is breached.

name: Cotton whitefly
symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck sap causing yellowing and leaf curling and excrete honeydew leading to sooty mould; also transmits leaf curl virus.
management: Use yellow sticky traps, avoid water/nitrogen stress and grow non-host trap crops; spray diafenthiuron 50 WP @ 1 g/litre or flonicamid 50 WG @ 0.3 g/litre.

name: Cotton jassid (leafhopper)
symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck sap from the leaf undersurface causing yellowing, downward curling and reddening of leaf margins known as hopper burn.
management: Grow hairy-leaved tolerant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen and conserve natural enemies; spray thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 0.2 g/litre or acetamiprid 20 SP @ 0.2 g/litre if the ETL is crossed.

name: Fall armyworm
symptoms: Larvae feed inside the whorl producing characteristic window-pane feeding and rows of round holes on unfurling leaves, with visible frass in the whorl.
management: Monitor with pheromone traps, hand-pick and destroy egg masses and apply sand/ash mixed with neem in the whorl; spray emamectin benzoate 5 SG @ 0.4 g/litre or spinetoram 11.7 SC @ 0.5 ml/litre directed into the whorl.

name: Maize stem borer
symptoms: Larvae bore into the whorl and stem causing shot holes on leaves and dead heart in young plants.
management: Remove and destroy stubble, use resistant/tolerant hybrids and release Trichogramma; apply carbofuran 3G @ 8-10 kg/ha in the whorl or spray chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @ 0.3 ml/litre.

name: Sugarcane early shoot borer
symptoms: Larvae bore into young shoots causing a central 'dead heart' that emits a foul smell and can be pulled out easily.
management: Use healthy setts, avoid late planting, earth up and mulch with trash; apply chlorantraniliprole 0.4 G @ 22.5 kg/ha or fipronil 0.3 G @ 25 kg/ha at planting/earthing-up.

name: Sugarcane red rot
symptoms: Internal reddening of the stalk with white cross patches and an alcoholic smell; leaves show drying from the tip.
management: Use disease-free setts of resistant varieties, hot-water treat setts at 50 C for 2 hours, avoid ratooning of infected fields and rogue affected clumps; drench soil with carbendazim 50 WP @ 1 g/litre where the disease recurs.

name: Pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera)
symptoms: Larvae bore into pods and feed on developing seeds, with the head thrust inside the pod while the body remains outside.
management: Install pheromone traps @ 5/ha, use bird perches and apply NPV @ 250 LE/ha while conserving natural enemies; spray emamectin benzoate 5 SG @ 0.4 g/litre or indoxacarb 14.5 SC @ 0.5 ml/litre at ETL of 1 larva/plant.

name: Pigeonpea wilt (Fusarium)
symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of plants usually after flowering, with characteristic blackening of the xylem visible on splitting the stem.
management: Grow resistant/tolerant varieties, follow a 3-year crop rotation avoiding pigeonpea and practise deep summer ploughing; treat seed with carbendazim 2 g/kg or Trichoderma viride 4 g/kg seed.

name: Soybean girdle beetle
symptoms: Adults girdle the stem/petiole in a ring causing the portion above to wilt and dry, while grubs tunnel inside the stem.
management: Remove and destroy girdled plant parts, follow crop rotation and deep-plough after harvest; spray thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 0.2 g/litre or chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @ 0.3 ml/litre at early infestation.

name: Soybean yellow mosaic virus
symptoms: Irregular yellow and green mosaic patches appear on leaves along with stunted growth and reduced pod formation; spread by whitefly.
management: Grow tolerant varieties, rogue infected plants early and control the whitefly vector using yellow sticky traps; spray thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 0.2 g/litre or flonicamid 50 WG @ 0.3 g/litre to check vector spread.

name: Groundnut leaf miner
symptoms: Larvae mine leaves forming serpentine galleries and later fold/web leaves, feeding from inside and causing drying of foliage.
management: Follow crop rotation, avoid moisture stress and conserve parasitoids; spray quinalphos 25 EC @ 2 ml/litre or novaluron 10 EC @ 1 ml/litre at early mining.

name: Groundnut tikka leaf spot
symptoms: Circular brown (early) or black (late) leaf spots with a yellow halo appear, causing defoliation and reduced pod filling.
management: Use resistant varieties, follow crop rotation and remove volunteer plants and debris; spray chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2 g/litre or tebuconazole 25.9 EC @ 1 ml/litre at first appearance, repeating at a 15-day interval.

name: Mustard aphid
symptoms: Colonies cluster on the inflorescence, tender shoots and pods sucking sap, causing curling, stunting and reduced seed set.
management: Grow early-sown/tolerant varieties, conserve coccinellid predators and intercrop with coriander; spray imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.3 ml/litre or dimethoate 30 EC @ 1.5 ml/litre when about 50 aphids/plant are crossed.

name: Mustard white rust
symptoms: White pustules form on the leaf undersurface and stem, with distortion and hypertrophy of the inflorescence known as staghead.
management: Use resistant varieties, follow crop rotation and remove and destroy staghead-affected plants; spray metalaxyl 8% + mancozeb 64% WP @ 2 g/litre at disease onset.

name: Potato late blight
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions form on leaf margins turning brown-black with white fungal growth on the undersurface in humid weather; tubers show reddish-brown dry rot.
management: Use disease-free seed tubers, earth up properly and avoid overhead irrigation in cloudy weather; spray mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/litre prophylactically and cymoxanil + mancozeb @ 3 g/litre on disease appearance.

name: Potato tuber moth
symptoms: Larvae mine leaves and bore into tubers in the field and storage, making galleries filled with frass that reduce tuber quality.
management: Ensure adequate earthing-up to prevent tuber exposure, use certified seed and store in cool ventilated conditions with neem-leaf layering; spray chlorpyriphos 20 EC @ 2.5 ml/litre or spinosad 45 SC @ 0.3 ml/litre at 15-day intervals near harvest.

name: Tomato early blight
symptoms: Concentric ring (target board) brown spots appear on older leaves, enlarging and causing defoliation from the bottom upward.
management: Use disease-free seed/transplants, follow crop rotation and avoid overhead irrigation, removing infected debris; spray mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/litre or azoxystrobin 23 SC @ 1 ml/litre at a 10-15 day interval.

name: Tomato leaf curl virus
symptoms: Upward curling and crinkling of leaves occur along with stunted bushy growth and reduced fruit set; transmitted by whitefly.
management: Use virus-tolerant varieties, raise nursery under insect-proof net and rogue infected plants early while controlling the whitefly vector; spray thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 0.2 g/litre or diafenthiuron 50 WP @ 1 g/litre.

name: Tomato fruit borer (Helicoverpa)
symptoms: Larvae bore round holes into fruits and feed inside, causing fruit rot and yield loss.
management: Install pheromone traps @ 5/ha, hand-pick damaged fruits and conserve natural enemies; spray emamectin benzoate 5 SG @ 0.4 g/litre or spinosad 45 SC @ 0.3 ml/litre at ETL.

name: Onion thrips
symptoms: Rasping-sucking damage causes silvery streaks and white patches on leaves along with curling and stunted bulb growth in heavy infestation.
management: Avoid water stress, use blue sticky traps and intercrop with coriander; spray fipronil 5 SC @ 1.5 ml/litre or spinosad 45 SC @ 0.3 ml/litre, alternating chemistries to avoid resistance.

name: Onion purple blotch
symptoms: Small water-soaked lesions on leaves enlarge into purplish concentric zoned spots, causing leaf blight and neck rot in storage.
management: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen and overhead irrigation, and maintain field sanitation; spray mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/litre or difenoconazole 25 EC @ 1 ml/litre at a 10-day interval.

name: Mango hopper
symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck sap from the inflorescence and tender shoots, excreting honeydew that causes sooty mould and flower/fruit drop.
management: Prune to maintain canopy openness, avoid dense planting and conserve natural enemies; spray imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.3 ml/litre or lambda-cyhalothrin 5 EC @ 1 ml/litre at panicle emergence.

name: Mango powdery mildew
symptoms: White powdery fungal growth appears on the inflorescence, young leaves and fruits, causing flower and fruit drop.
management: Prune for aeration and avoid a dense canopy; spray wettable sulphur 80 WP @ 2 g/litre or hexaconazole 5 EC @ 2 ml/litre at panicle emergence, repeating at a 15-day interval.

name: Banana sigatoka leaf spot
symptoms: Yellowish streaks on leaves develop into brown-black elongated spots with a yellow halo, coalescing and drying large leaf areas and reducing bunch weight.
management: Remove and destroy affected leaves, ensure proper drainage and spacing for aeration; spray propiconazole 25 EC @ 1 ml/litre or carbendazim 50 WP @ 1 g/litre at 3-4 week intervals.

name: Citrus canker
symptoms: Raised corky brown lesions with oily/water-soaked margins appear on leaves, twigs and fruits; severe infection causes defoliation and fruit drop.
management: Use disease-free planting material, control citrus leaf miner which creates entry wounds, prune and destroy affected twigs and avoid overhead irrigation; spray copper oxychloride 50 WP @ 3 g/litre with streptocycline 500 ppm.

name: Grapes downy mildew
symptoms: Yellowish oily patches appear on the upper leaf surface with white cottony fungal growth on the undersurface in humid weather, affecting shoots and berries.
management: Ensure canopy management for aeration, avoid overhead irrigation and remove affected leaves; spray metalaxyl 8% + mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/litre or fosetyl-Al 80 WP @ 2.5 g/litre at disease onset.

name: Chilli thrips
symptoms: Rasping-sucking damage causes upward curling of leaves as part of a leaf curl complex, with silvery streaks, stunted growth and reduced fruit set.
management: Use reflective mulch, avoid excess nitrogen and grow maize as a barrier crop; spray fipronil 5 SC @ 1.5 ml/litre or spinetoram 11.7 SC @ 0.5 ml/litre.

name: Brinjal shoot and fruit borer
symptoms: Larvae bore into shoots causing wilting of terminal shoots and later bore into fruits, leaving frass-plugged entry holes that make fruit unfit for sale.
management: Clip and destroy wilted shoots and infested fruits regularly, install pheromone traps @ 12/ha and grow resistant varieties; spray chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @ 0.3 ml/litre or spinosad 45 SC @ 0.3 ml/litre.

name: Okra yellow vein mosaic virus
symptoms: Vein clearing is followed by a network of yellow veins on leaves, with small pale yellow/white fruits in severe infection; transmitted by whitefly.
management: Grow tolerant varieties such as Arka Anamika, rogue infected plants early and control the whitefly vector; spray thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 0.2 g/litre or diafenthiuron 50 WP @ 1 g/litre.

name: Apple scab
symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots appear on leaves and fruit, causing cracking, deformity and premature fruit drop.
management: Prune for canopy aeration and remove and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to reduce inoculum; spray captan 50 WP @ 2 g/litre or myclobutanil 10 WP @ 1 g/litre from pink bud stage at 10-14 day intervals.

name: Coffee berry borer
symptoms: The adult female bores a hole near the calyx end of berries and lays eggs; larvae tunnel inside destroying beans and causing premature berry drop.
management: Practise timely and thorough harvesting including gleaning of fallen/residual berries and use Broca traps with alcohol-methanol lure; apply Beauveria bassiana or a spinosad-based bait spray during peak infestation.
